🌡️ Volatility Regime Detector live

Ranks the current ATR(14) against its own trailing 200-bar distribution — a percentile, not a fixed number, so "high volatility" means the same thing on a quiet pair as a wild one. When auto-adapt is on, the live Auto Refresh cadence (top of the Price Chart) tightens to 1.5s in Extreme conditions and relaxes to 5s when things are quiet, instead of a fixed 3s regardless of how fast the market is actually moving.

🔀 SMMA Cross Signal SMMA(12) shift 0 / shift 6

Two Smoothed Moving Averages, period 12 — one plotted at the current bar (shift 0), the other displaced 6 bars forward (shift 6), same as the classic MT4 shifted-MA setup. Watch for the two lines crossing, and for price crossing above/below either line.

📏 Volatility (Candle Size) SMMA Cross SMMA(12) on bar range

Same shift-0/shift-6 SMMA technique as the price cross above, but applied to each bar's range (high−low) instead of its close — a leading read on volatility turning, distinct from the Volatility Regime Detector's percentile snapshot of where volatility currently sits. Shift-0 crossing above shift-6 means recent candles are growing faster than the smoothed projection (expansion beginning); crossing below means they're shrinking (contraction/cooling off).

🎯 Per-Combo Auto-Optimizer — Asset × Timeframe × Strategy idle V66.1

Per-Combo Auto-Optimizer — runs an INDEPENDENT walk-forward optimization for every watchlist asset × every selected timeframe × all 4 strategies (V60 + SMC + 4-Ind + Fusion). Each combo gets its own tuned entry gates (RSI zone · ADX floor · DI alignment · Fusion conviction · AI confluence floor), optimized for the ≥60% win-rate target under the unified V64 ratchet ladder (BE@+1R → 0R, +2R → +1R, +3R → +2R …). Best practices built in: 70/30 in-sample/out-of-sample walk-forward validation, minimum sample size, profit-factor & net-R guards, coarse grids against overfitting, and every strategy's identity floors (pattern counts, conviction minimums, trend checks) always preserved — the optimizer only tunes the per-combo gates the data supports. WR* = win rate excluding breakeven scratches — exits with |R| ≤ 0.05 (BE-lock exits and stalled-flat scratches) count in NEITHER wins nor losses; Net R and PF still include every trade. Statuses: ✅ = walk-forward validated at/above target (needs ≥10 decisive trades) · ✅ OOS⚠ = target hit in-sample but out-of-sample was weak (config kept, flagged) · ⚠ best = best sample-supported config below target · ⏳ = insufficient trade sample — combo keeps the strategy baseline · ⏸ = candles loaded but the strategy fired no signals in that window · ❌ = no candle data for that symbol/TF (connect the MT5 bridge or a live source). Once a combo is tabulated and tuned its parameters — including the AI confluence floor — are auto-saved into ALL live and test trading paths: chart signals, MTF scan, watchlist auto-trade, bridge execution, exit-bias gate, manual-order SSOT, the Backtest Suite (single + multi-TF + AUTH) and the forward/paper test all read the same tuned store through mxComboCfg() in the 4 signal generators, saved to localStorage the moment each combo is tuned, picked up by other terminal tabs automatically, and restored at boot. The 🧠 AI-Precision Core (verdicts · lessons · exit precision) reads the same store and the local confluence engine. “Reset Params” clears them everywhere. 🐍 Bridge Setup — Manual, Human-Confirmed Execution

All three options below only ever execute a single order after you click Confirm & Send in this terminal. None of them scan for signals or trade on their own — the terminal does the analysis, a human clicks Confirm, and the bridge relays that one order.

Talks to MT5's native Python API directly. Runs a local WebSocket server this terminal connects to; every order it places is one you clicked Confirm on.

  1. Click Download mt5_bridge.py below
  2. Run pip install MetaTrader5 websockets
  3. Open MT5, log into your account (demo or live)
  4. Run python mt5_bridge.py — leave it running. Now with autonomous mode: if the terminal disconnects, the bridge continues managing open positions (breakeven, SL ratchet, reversal close) until you reconnect.
  5. Back here, click Connect Bridge — status turns green
  6. Every BUY/SELL/Confirm click sends exactly one order for you to have already approved in the popup

Alternative to the Python route: an Expert Advisor that watches a local command file. Use this if you can't install Python on the trading machine.

  1. Download ApexBridge_MT5.mq5 and mt5_bridge.py (relay mode)
  2. Copy the .mq5 file into your MT5 MQL5/Experts folder, compile it in MetaEditor, and drag it onto one chart
  3. Enable AutoTrading (top toolbar) so the EA is allowed to execute the orders you approve
  4. Run python mt5_bridge.py --relay on the same machine — it writes the command file the EA reads and relays positions back to this terminal
  5. Connect Bridge here — every Confirm click writes one command file; the EA opens exactly that one trade and nothing else

MT4 has no native Python API, so this uses the same file-relay pattern: the local Python relay writes one command file per Confirmed order, the EA executes only that file's order, then reports back.

  1. Download ApexBridge_MT4.mq4 and mt5_bridge.py (relay mode — works for MT4 too, just talks in files instead of the MT5 API)
  2. Copy the .mq4 file into your MT4 MQL4/Experts folder, compile in MetaEditor, drag onto a chart
  3. Enable AutoTrading and allow DLL/file imports for the EA (needed only to read/write the local command files — not to auto-generate trades)
  4. Run python mt5_bridge.py --relay --mt4 on the same machine
  5. Connect Bridge here — each Confirm click produces one command file → one executed order → one status update back to the position table
